entries.disposition: Empty fallback in digest hash validation has the same invalid-digest outcome. coverage-audit.test.mjs 257-271 rejects invalid snapshot/artifact byte counts and hashes before publication.
Empty fallback in source-file hash validation has the same closed source-metadata rejection outcome. coverage-audit.test.mjs 259-260 verifies invalid source bytes and hashes publish no audit.

Exact raw/source file counts are required first; unknown, ambiguous and duplicate mappings are rejected. Every accepted raw file adds one unique known source, making the final mapped-size inequality unreachable. Missing and duplicate raw sources are tested.
strictArtifactRef admits only nonempty relative basenames, so the resolved artifact cannot escape its root. coverage-audit.test.mjs 273-274 rejects traversal and nested references.
Basename references and readRegular rejection of symlinks/non-files ensure immutable regular artifact children resolve within the canonical artifact root; this repeats the containment guard.

Codeless adapter_failure fallback is unreachable: executable admission, adapterCommand, invokeAdapter and assertAdmission failures carry codes; runPackageCommand child failures are classified by invokeAdapter. bootstrap.test.mjs 1055-1064 verifies version admission failure and independent preflight checks.
Admission at 424-432 requires mutually exclusive fixture_predicate shapes for inject-mode-protocol-error-once and reject-mode; their conjunction is rejected before this guard.
Recovery variations at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:47-78 and 126-180 own missing/malformed argument proof and changed projections; an absent request has the same no-recovery outcome.
validRecoveryContext at 709-720 requires contiguous ranges covering zero through calls.length; every iterated call index belongs to exactly one range.
All admitted request/response objects come from JSON.parse through parseFrame; JSON objects cannot have a null prototype.
The only compactPending caller checks Array.isArray(payload.pending) first, so the non-array fallback cannot execute.

Partial-handshake test tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:764-796 proves invalid program path disables fixture injection and preserves the original request; an omitted final operand has the same outcome.
Backpressure tests at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:655-683 and 994-1004 prove accepted output drains before exit; queued waiters at final callback depend on scheduling.
Existing backpressure tests own wait-for-output; entering the promise arm depends on child-close versus stdout-callback scheduling.
Publication-failure test tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:867-891 owns controlled teardown without unhandled error; later queued failures are idempotent re-entry at the same boundary.
SIGTERM, SIGKILL fallback and owner-loss tests at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:1084-1114 own child termination; repeated stop is an idempotent teardown race.
Oversized-input tests at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:961-979 own fail-closed input teardown; later buffered stdin discard is the same boundary.

Oversized-provider-frame and publication-failure tests at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:867-891 and 981-992 own absence of partial output/evidence; late buffered stdout belongs to that teardown boundary.
Backpressure tests at tests/cursor-skill-eval.test.mjs:655-683 and 994-1004 own output-drain promise; resolver callback execution is scheduler-dependent.
